Reservoir borrow area operation - Howard Creek will be protected

) from construction runoff from borrow areas using sediment basins in Bad Creek and West Bad Creek as shown on drawing PBK-1014-2. Runoff from the borrow areas will be held in the basins for plain sedimentation. The basins will then discharge the water into Howard Creek. Table III on drawing PBK-1014-2 lists basin capacities. A typical basin is shown on Figure 1. Operations within the borrow area will be conducted to minimize erosion. Clearing will be done on a yearly basis opening up only the area needed for that year. Runoff will be directed into sediment basins. Terraces and diversions will be used where nocessary. Sediment basin dike slopes will be stabilized upon completion using permanent vegetation. Silt fences, brush barriers or other means of retaining sediment will be used downstream of the dikes during dike construction. When borrow areas are depleted, exposed soil above full pond elevation 2310 will be stabilized by grading and sowing of permanent vegetation.
All of the borrow areas lie within the Bad Creek and West Bad Creek drainage areas except part of the supplemental borrow area which lies within the Whitewater River drainage basin. If the supplemental borrow area is required, the boundary within the Whitewater basin will be at elevation 2315 as shown on drawing PBK-1014-2. A drainage ditch will be placed along this boundary to collect runoff from the borrow area and divert it back into the Bad Creek drainage basin.
Excavation of the intake channel will take place after the sediment basin is built in Bad Creek. Runoff from the intake channel will be diverted into the Bad Creek basin for plain sedimentation.
c) Construction Yard and Switchyard - Runoff from the construction yard and switchyard will be controlled using a sediment basin as shown on drawing PBK-1014-2. The surfaces of the yards will be sloped to direct runoff into the basin for plain sedimentation. Basin capacities are given in Table III on drawing PBK-1014-2. The outlet from the basin will run beneath the switchyard and discharge into a local stream. The outlet configuration will be similar to that shown on Figure 1.During construction of the switchyard, runoff from the fill slopes will be directed through silt fences, brush barriers or other structures to remove sediment. These slopes will be stabilized with permanent vegetation as soon as practical. Yard drains will discharge into the sediment basin.
d) Embankment Construction
Main Dam - Erosion and sediment pollution during construction of the Main Dam will be controlled in part by incremental clearing and grubbing of the dam foundation on a yearly basis.
